title: Process Handoff Pack
learningObjective: Shape a package another analyst could reuse tomorrow without inheriting hidden assumptions.
lifecycleCue: This pack highlights how Shaping supports Deployment and repeatable use.
caseBrief: A finance operations manager wants a reusable monthly close handoff package for another analyst. The package must separate the official procedure from informal notes, keep the current due date visible, and define what to do if a required source is missing.
successCriteria: The official procedure remains easy to find and reuse.
The package explicitly distinguishes current run facts from general procedure.
The CHECKS make the artifact safe for handoff and repeated use.
outputReminder: Did the response produce a reusable handoff artifact instead of a vague summary?
Did it keep informal notes from overriding the official procedure?
Did it say what to do if a required source was missing?

precedenceRules.label: Official procedure and exception rules outrank informal notes.
Recent informal notes from the prior analyst win.

handlingOptions.label: Flag the missing source and stop for review.
Work around the missing source with best judgment.
Guess the missing source and continue.

blocks.label: Process Handoff Designer
blocks.text: Act as a process handoff designer creating a package another analyst can reuse. Optimize for legibility, repeatability, and reviewability.

blocks.label: Make It Reusable
blocks.text: Write for a different analyst, not just for yourself. Keep steps, sources, and checks explicit enough that another person can run the workflow without hidden assumptions.

blocks.label: Separate Procedure from Notes
blocks.text: Treat informal notes as context, not authority. The official procedure and exception rules remain the governing sources.

blocks.label: Official Monthly Close Procedure
blocks.text: Official procedure excerpt: reconcile exception queue, validate late invoices, post approved adjustments, and publish the close summary after the checklist is complete.

blocks.label: Exception Rule Note
blocks.text: Official exception rule: if a late invoice source file is missing, the analyst must pause the close summary and notify the finance manager before posting adjustments.

blocks.label: Informal Prior-Analyst Notes
blocks.text: Informal note: 'If the queue looks normal, I usually skip the manager message and post anyway.' This note is not an approved rule.

blocks.label: Current Run Facts
blocks.text: Dynamic facts: the monthly close summary is due tomorrow at 11:00 AM. The late-invoice source file has not arrived yet.

blocks.label: Create the Handoff Envelope
blocks.text: Task: prepare a reusable handoff package for the next analyst that explains the work, the approved inputs, the sequence, and what to do if the missing source still does not arrive.

blocks.label: Handoff Artifact Format
blocks.text: Output expectation: return sections titled Objective, Required Inputs, Steps, and Checks.

blocks.label: Missing-Source Stop Rule
blocks.text: Checks: if the source file is still missing, say the handoff cannot continue to posting and must pause for manager review.

rationale.ROLE: Frame the package as a handoff artifact, not a one-off answer.
rationale.RULES: Make reuse and authority explicit before the procedure appears.
rationale.REFERENCE: Keep official procedure visible and demote the informal shortcut note.
rationale.DYNAMIC FACTS: Current due date and missing-file status belong in a run-specific block.
rationale.TASK: Name the deliverable clearly for the next analyst.
rationale.OUTPUT: Use a reusable structure another person can review fast.
rationale.CHECKS: Protect repeatable use with a pause condition.

exploreMore.prompt: Remove the CHECKS block and compare the package. What risk becomes invisible?

branches.title: No-CHECKS comparison
branches.instruction: Delete CHECKS, rerun, and compare what reviewers can no longer inspect quickly.
branches.watchFor: Whether verification and refresh duties become vague.
branches.why: This isolates why CHECKS matter for repeated use.

branches.title: Compress for a busy teammate
branches.instruction: Trim one block without losing handoff readiness, then explain the tradeoff.
branches.watchFor: Whether the package stays reusable by someone else.
branches.why: This forces clarity under time pressure.

build: Shape the package so another person could pick it up without hidden assumptions.
Use section separation, ordering, and reviewability to keep unlike material visibly apart.
Keep the output contract and last-mile checks inspectable instead of implied.
copy: Before running externally, ask whether a teammate who did not design the package would still know what must be verified next.
Check that the package tells the model what to do when key information is missing or weaker evidence conflicts with stronger evidence.
review: Did the result read like a reusable handoff artifact instead of a personal note?
Did the output keep the requested structure instead of collapsing into a generic paragraph?
Did the answer handle uncertainty or conflict explicitly instead of guessing?
